translation.english_title: Shattered is my love's living portrait

english_lines: Shattered is my love's living portrait,
Destroyed is the epic of flavour in my life.
notes: `உயிரோவியம்` remains the striking `living portrait` image rather than becoming simply `my beloved`.
`சுவைக் காவியம்` is kept close as `epic of flavour`; smoothing it to `beautiful story` would erase the unusual source metaphor.

english_lines: Shattered is my love's living portrait,
Destroyed is the epic of flavour in my life.
notes: The source places these lines under the Thogaiyara performance structure; the English retains the same lyric wording rather than rewriting the repeated passage.

english_lines: The heart-enchanting life, the flame of life, slips away hidden...
A storm blows... in the flower-garden...
notes: The source's `ஜீவன் / வாழ்வின் ஜோதி` accumulation remains doubled rather than compressed into one `life is fading` sentence.
The storm remains inside the concrete flower-garden image.

english_lines: The divine statue of love where grace dwells has fallen...
My life has become an empty temple,
notes: The fallen deity-statue / empty-temple sequence is preserved intact; it is the central architectural-spiritual image of the stanza.
The verified source form `வெறுங்` is not normalized in Tamil; the English follows its empty/bare-temple sense.

translator_notes: The song's grief is carried through painting, epic, flame, storm, flower-garden, divine statue and empty-temple images; the English retains those images instead of replacing them with generalized heartbreak.
No separate singer is inferred from outside the verified Tamil record.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
